claims.statement: AI Act Article 4 obligations have applied since 2 February 2025 and require providers and deployers to support context-appropriate AI literacy.
AI use rose to 20% of EU enterprises in 2025 while Poland remained at 8.4%, indicating adoption is growing from a relatively low Polish base.
Likely payers are HR, compliance, or information-security owners already funding training; willingness to buy an evidence ledger rather than generic courses is unknown.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: HR, compliance, data-protection, or information-security lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Learning-management systems can bundle courses; role-specific assessments, policy attestations, and AI-use evidence are the wedge
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct employer subscriptions
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: HR consultants, DPOs, cyber advisers, and targeted outbound

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual subscription in advance plus paid setup
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 75-85% after content review and support
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 10-30 setup hours plus quarterly content maintenance
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Legal-content review, security, GDPR, and insurance; exact cost unknown
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Assessment inference, hosting, support, and specialist content review

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: LMS and compliance vendors add AI-literacy modules and attestations
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current staff and adviser time spent training employees, collecting attestations, and demonstrating role-appropriate AI literacy
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: AI rollout, customer audit, board risk review, or missing training evidence
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual reassessment and onboarding of new staff

contrary_evidence: The Commission says the obligation does not impose one prescribed individual literacy level.
Generic training content is abundant and cheap.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed workflow-integration agreement with an employer's identity and training systems; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Provide standalone assessments and downloadable evidence without integration
critical_control_point.current_owner: Employers own staff records and LMS workflows; no access is currently held
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct employer subscriptions
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Public regulatory material supports product development; no employer data or internal Reckitt material is usable
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business controls standalone assessment delivery; employer controls staff assignment and records
critical_control_point.subject: Role-specific AI-literacy assessment and evidence workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Build three role-specific Polish assessments, pilot with small professional-service employers, then add LMS integration
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 500 employers averaging 12,000 PLN ARR produces 6m PLN ARR; at 25% owner earnings or a recurring-software valuation, founder net worth could exceed 5m PLN in 5-8 years. Competitive pricing and renewal are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly after initial content build
economics.gross_margin_basis: Subscription less hosting, support, and recurring legal/content review
economics.payback: Assumption: 6-10 months at 6,000 PLN acquisition cost and 750 PLN monthly contribution
economics.pricing: Assumption: 6,000-30,000 PLN annually by employee count
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual plus new-hire and role-change assessments

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Benchmark data linking roles, AI uses, knowledge gaps, and remediation
fingerprint.customer: Polish employers deploying generative or predictive AI
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Compliance or HR pays for training administration and demonstrable evidence
fingerprint.problem_trigger: AI use is rising while a literacy obligation already applies

founder_fit: Founder understands AI deployment and can create technical assessments.
Recurring evidence workflows favor automation over live training.
Delivery avoids camera dependence and constant networking.
risks: LMS vendors can bundle the workflow.
Buyers may accept simple attendance records.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: role based ai literacy evidence ledger
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: employer acceptance of structured evidence beyond course attendance

structure.control_point: Role-specific assessment record integrated into onboarding

thesis: Growing workplace AI use plus an already-applicable literacy duty creates recurring demand for evidence, not merely another generic course.
title: AI-Literacy Evidence Ledger
uncertainties: Polish buyers' training budgets are unknown.
Whether assessments materially outperform LMS attestations is unknown.
